'''Anthony Erwin Randolph Jr.''' (born July 15, 1989) is an American and naturalized Slovenian former professional [[basketball]] player. He represented the senior [[Slovenia national basketball team|Slovenian national basketball team]], winning the [[2017 EuroBasket]] with them. Born in Germany to two American parents who served in the [[US military]] there, Randolph's family eventually relocated to the United States, where he grew up in [[Pasadena, California]]. The family later moved to [[Dallas]], [[Texas]], where Randolph soon became a standout at [[Woodrow Wilson High School (Dallas, Texas)|Woodrow Wilson High School]], eventually being recruited by the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU Tigers]]. After one year, Randolph left college, and entered the [[2008 NBA draft]], where he was chosen as the fourteenth pick overall by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. In [[2015–16 Euroleague|2016]], he earned an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] selection.

==Early life==
Anthony Erwin Randolph Jr. was born to Anthony and Crystal Randolph in [[Würzburg]], [[West Germany]], where both of his parents served in the US military.<ref name="ARNBABio">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/anthony_randolph/|title=Anthony Randolph Stats, Video, Bio, Profile|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 13, 2013}}</ref> Randolph spent the first year of his life in Germany, before his family moved to [[Pasadena, California]], where he spent the majority of his childhood.<ref name="ARNBABio" /> Randolph attended schools in Pasadena, as well as [[North Little Rock High School]], in [[North Little Rock, Arkansas]], before heading to [[Woodrow Wilson High School (Dallas, Texas)|Woodrow Wilson High School]], in [[Dallas]], Texas, for his junior year.<ref name="ARNewsFellow">{{cite web|url=http://www.newsfollow.com/the-raw-feed/anthony-randolph|title=Anthony Randolph Pictures, News and Video — NewsFollow|publisher=NewsFollow.com|access-date=2009-07-13}}</ref>

Randolph's mother decided the school he was attending in Arkansas, was not right for him because of the differences he had with the team's [[head coach]] and in school.<ref name="WWPatWashingtonIntrvw">{{cite news|url=http://www.warriorsworld.net/news/latest/interview-with-pat-washington---anthony-randolphs-high-school-coach.html|title=Warriorsworld — Interview with Pat Washington — Anthony Randolph's High School Coach|date=2009-06-29|access-date=2009-07-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090711154401/http://www.warriorsworld.net/news/latest/interview-with-pat-washington---anthony-randolphs-high-school-coach.html|archive-date=July 11, 2009|url-status=dead|publisher=WarriorsWorld.net}}</ref> At the time, he was a virtually unknown player.<ref name="WWPatWashingtonIntrvw" /> Pat Washington, Randolph's high school head coach, stated that while Randolph was athletically gifted, he needed a lot of work on skills, such as ball handling, shooting, etc.<ref name="WWPatWashingtonIntrvw" /> Washington also spoke of a technique the team had in workouts called the "LAB", where the basic rules were that all players in play were required to never stop running, under any circumstances, and if the ball was turned over at any point, the player was to run back on defense immediately.<ref name="WWPatWashingtonIntrvw" /> The technique might have contributed to Randolph's later defensive prowess, as he has been known to hustle back after [[Turnover (basketball)|turnovers]], for defensive stops, in his professional career.

In high school, Randolph played all five positions on the floor.<ref name="WWPatWashingtonIntrvw" /> During his senior season, Randolph's team did not qualify for a playoff position, which coach Washington attributed to bad chemistry.<ref name="WWPatWashingtonIntrvw" /> Washington called the team very talented, and referred to Randolph as the best player on the roster, but stated that, "as time went by, jealousy and agendas set in and took over."<ref name="WWPatWashingtonIntrvw" /> Randolph averaged 25.8 points and 12.6 rebounds per game, as a senior.<ref name="ARNewsFellow" /> Although Randolph was named to the first team All-Area ''[[The Dallas Morning News]]'' boys basketball team, played in the [[Reebok]] Round Ball Classic, in [[Chicago]], and the [[Kentucky Derby Festival Basketball Classic|Adidas Derby Festival Classic]] in [[Kentucky]] (leading all scorers in both games), he was not chosen to play in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]] his senior year.<ref name="ARNewsFellow" /><ref name="WWPatWashingtonIntrvw" /> Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Randolph was listed as the No. 4 [[small forward]] and the No. 12 player in the nation in 2007.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Anthony-Randolph-42273 Anthony Randolph Recruiting Profile]</ref>

==College career==
[[Glen Davis (basketball)|Glen Davis]] had just left [[Louisiana State University]]'s basketball team as well as seven-foot center [[Magnum Rolle]], who transferred to [[Louisiana Tech University|Louisiana Tech]], leaving the team with only two bigs, one being a [[junior college]] transfer.<ref name="WWPatWashingtonIntrvw" /> Due to this fact, LSU told Randolph that if he joined their team, he could possibly play right away as a freshman.<ref name="WWPatWashingtonIntrvw" /> Washington said that [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] were also interested in recruiting Randolph.<ref name="WWPatWashingtonIntrvw" /> Though Memphis was Randolph's early choice in the recruitment process, he wanted to attend a school where he could play big minutes, which he figured he probably would not get to do at Memphis since the team's roster was so deep at the time.<ref name="WWPatWashingtonIntrvw" /> Randolph made an impact in college right away, as he had six blocks in just his third game during his freshman season.<ref name="ARNewsFellow" /> During his lone season at LSU, Randolph earned Honorable Mention All-SEC and First Team All-Freshman Team honors.<ref name="Warriors2008NBADraft">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/Warriors_2008_Draft_Release.html|title=WARRIORS: Warriors Add Anthony Randolph And Richard Hendrix In 2008 NBA Draft|work=NBA.com|access-date=2009-07-13}}</ref> Randolph was the only LSU Tiger to start all thirty-one games in his freshman season, and averaged 15.6 [[Point (basketball)|points]], 8.5 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], 1.2 assists, 1.13 steals, and 2.26 [[Block (basketball)|blocks]] per contest.<ref name="ARNewsFellow" /><ref name="Warriors2008NBADraft" /> Although the team only ended the season with a 13–18 record, Randolph finished strong by averaging 20.1 points during the last nine games of the year.<ref name="ARNewsFellow" /> Randolph also ranked third in the [[Southeastern Conference]] in rebounding and blocked shots, twelfth in scoring, and posted nine [[Double (basketball)#Double-double|double-doubles]] his freshman season.<ref name="Warriors2008NBADraft" />

==Professional career==
===Golden State Warriors (2008–2010)===
[[Image:Anthony Randolph cropped.jpg|thumb|left|Randolph with the Golden State Warriors in 2009]]
Knowing there was a good chance he would be chosen in the first round, Randolph declared himself eligible for the [[2008 NBA draft]] at the end of his freshman year at LSU.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/story/10767874|title=LSU's Randolph declares himself eligible for NBA Draft — NCAA Division I Mens Basketball — CBSS|work=[[CBSSports.com]]|access-date=2009-07-15}}</ref> Some projected Randolph to go high in the year's draft because of his versatility and potential, while his detractors thought he might drop because of his thin frame and raw overall game.<ref name="NBADraftnet">{{cite web|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/anthony-randolph|title=Anthony Randolph — NBADraft.net|publisher=NBADraft.net|access-date=2009-07-13| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090623052454/http://www.nbadraft.net/players/anthony-randolph| archive-date= 23 June 2009 | url-status= live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Chad Ford's Mock Draft, Version 6.0: Picks 1-30 - NBA — ESPN|last=Ford|first=Chad|work=ESPN.com|date=2008-06-23|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2008/columns/story?columnist=ford_chad&page=MockDraft-080623|access-date=2009-07-15}}</ref> In either case, many believed Randolph could be the steal of the draft with his talent and tremendous potential.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoopsaddict.com/2008/06/10/an-inside-look-at-anthony-randolph |title=Hoops Addict >> An Inside Look At Anthony Randolph |publisher=HoopsAddict.com |access-date=2009-07-15 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090401050422/http://www.hoopsaddict.com/2008/06/10/an-inside-look-at-anthony-randolph/ |archive-date=April 1, 2009 }}</ref>

In the draft, the [[Golden State Warriors]] selected Randolph with the fourteenth overall pick.<ref name="Warriors2008NBADraft" /> The Warriors were coming off a disappointing [[2007-08 NBA season|2007-08 season]] where the team was unable to qualify for the [[NBA Playoffs|playoffs]] despite finishing the year with a 48–34 win–loss record.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/GSW/2008.html|title=2007-08 Golden State Warriors Roster and Statistics — Basketball-Reference.com|publisher=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=2009-07-13}}</ref> Early in his rookie season, Randolph received minimal playing time, causing some to question his attitude and work ethic, or if a possible rift might be developing between him and head coach [[Don Nelson]].<ref>{{cite news|title=SFGate : Randolph hopes to work his way out of doghouse|last=Hu|first=Janny|newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle|SFGate.com]]|date=2009-01-04|url=https://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/Randolph-hopes-to-work-his-way-out-of-doghouse-3178144.php|access-date=2009-07-15}}</ref> Many of the Warriors' main rotation players suffered injuries throughout Randolph's rookie campaign, and the team ended the season with only a 29–53 record.<ref name="GSW0809SsnRvw">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/200809_season_in_review.html|title=WARRIORS: 2008-09 Season In Review|work=NBA.com|access-date=2009-07-18}}</ref> Nonetheless, the Warriors did play a fairly strong second half of the season, including Randolph, who averaged 13.5 points, 10.5 rebounds, 1.6 blocks, and 1.4 steals over the last twelve games of the year.<ref name="GSW0809SsnRvw" />

After attending a [[Dallas Mavericks]]-[[San Antonio Spurs]] playoff game during the Warriors' offseason, Randolph became motivated to improve his play, hitting the gym hard to prepare for the following season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Randolph bigger, vows to be better — ContraCostaTimes.com|last=Thompson II|first=Marcus|publisher=[[Contra Costa Times|ContraCostaTimes.com]]|date=2009-06-15|url=http://www.contracostatimes.com/ci_12596651?source=rss&nclick_check=1|access-date=2009-07-15}}</ref> Randolph's efforts first began to reward him in that year's [[NBA Summer League|Summer League]] being held in [[Las Vegas Valley|Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]], where he not only began to dominate consistently but was also referred to by various sportswriters as being the best talent in the entire Summer League.<ref>{{cite news|title=Saturday Summer League Roundup — TrueHoop By Henry Abbott — ESPN |last=Arnovitz |first=Kevin |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=2009-07-12 |url=http://myespn.go.com/blogs/truehoop/0-42-60/Saturday-Summer-League-Roundup.html |access-date=2009-07-15 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090715095833/http://myespn.go.com/blogs/truehoop/0-42-60/Saturday-Summer-League-Roundup.html |archive-date=2009-07-15 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Kawakami|first=Tim|url=http://blogs.mercurynews.com/kawakami/2009/07/15/randolphs-42-its-just-summer-league-but-yes-hes-a-major-warriors-centerpiece|title=Randolph's 42: It's just Summer League, but yes, he's a major Warriors centerpiece : Talking Points|newspaper=[[San Jose Mercury News]]|access-date=2009-07-18}}</ref> Among other highlights, including a then-Summer League record-tying 42-point explosion in game four against the [[Chicago Bulls]]' Summer League team, Randolph was invited to attend the [[United States men's national basketball team|USA Basketball Men's National Team]] mini-camp following his dominant Summer League performance.<ref>{{cite news|title=NBA.com Randolph Ravages Bulls For 42 Points|work=NBA.com|date=2009-07-14|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague2009/games/20090714/GSWCHI/recap.html|access-date=2009-07-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=WARRIORS: Anthony Randolph Invited To Attend USA Basketball Mini-Camp|work=NBA.com|date=2009-07-20|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/randolph_team_usa_minicamp_072009.html|access-date=2009-07-22}}</ref> Though many believed Randolph was a lock to win Summer League MVP, the honor was given to [[2009 NBA draft|2009]] [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] [[Blake Griffin]].<ref>{{cite magazine|title=SLAM ONLINE : >> Even the Summer League Has an MVP 'Controversy'|last=Mutoni|first=Marcel|magazine=[[SLAM Magazine]]|date=2009-07-20|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/nba/2009/07/even-the-summer-league-has-an-mvp-controversy|access-date=2009-07-22}}</ref> On October 14, 2009, the Warriors extended Randolph's contract through the 2010–11 NBA season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2009/news/10/14/warriors.moves.ap/index.html|title=NBA.com: Warriors exercise their options on Wright, Randolph|work=NBA.com|access-date=2009-10-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091016054757/http://www.nba.com/2009/news/10/14/warriors.moves.ap/index.html|archive-date=16 October 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2010–2011)===
On July 9, 2010, Randolph was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] along with [[Kelenna Azubuike]], [[Ronny Turiaf]] and a future second-round pick in a [[sign and trade]] deal for [[David Lee (basketball)|David Lee]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/randolph_acquired070910.html|title=Knicks Acquire Randolph, Azubuike & Turiaf|date=July 9, 2010|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=July 9, 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100712051003/http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/randolph_acquired070910.html| archive-date= 12 July 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2011–2012)===
[[File:Anthony Randolph.jpg|thumb|Randolph with the Minnesota Timberwolves in 2011]]
On February 22, 2011, Randolph was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in a three-way blockbuster deal which also involved the [[Denver Nuggets]] that brought [[Carmelo Anthony]] to New York.<ref>{{cite web | title = Wolves Acquire Anthony Randolph | url = http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/pressrelease_Wolves_Acquire_Anthony_Randolph_2011_02_22.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2011-02-22 | access-date = 2011-02-23}}</ref> In his first start of the year on March 24, filling in for the injured [[Kevin Love]], Randolph recorded a career high 31 points and 11 rebounds. He followed that up with 24 points and 15 rebounds.

===Denver Nuggets (2012–2014)===
On July 20, 2012, Randolph signed a multi-year contract with the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-sign-free-agent-f-anthony-randolph|title=Denver Nuggets sign free-agent F Anthony Randolph|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 20, 2012|access-date=July 20, 2012}}</ref>

On June 26, 2014, Randolph was traded, along with [[Doug McDermott]], to the [[Chicago Bulls]] for [[Gary Harris]], [[Jusuf Nurkić]] and a 2015 second-round pick.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-acquire-mcdermott-draft-night-trade BULLS ACQUIRE MCDERMOTT VIA DRAFT NIGHT TRADE]</ref><ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20140627043621/http://www.chicagonow.com/bullsville/2014/06/anthony-randolph-acquired-by-bulls-in-mcdermott-trade/|title=Anthony Randolph acquired by Bulls in McDermott trade}}</ref>

On July 14, 2014, he was traded, along with two future second round draft picks and cash considerations, to the [[Orlando Magic]] in exchange for the draft rights to forward [[Milovan Raković]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-acquires-two-second-round-picks-chicago Orlando Acquires Two Second Round Picks From Chicago]</ref> The next day, he was waived by the Magic.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/127485/magic-waive-anthony-randolph.html |title=Magic waive Anthony Randolph |access-date=2014-08-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140819084737/http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/127485/magic-waive-anthony-randolph.html |archive-date=2014-08-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://www.orlandopinstripedpost.com/2014/7/15/5902953/2014-nba-free-agents-anthony-randolph-orlando-magic-waive NBA free agency 2014: Orlando Magic waive Anthony Randolph]</ref>

===Lokomotiv Kuban (2014–2016)===
On August 18, 2014, Randolph signed a one-year deal with [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]] of Russia.<ref>{{cite news|title=Lokomotiv Kuban adds big man Randolph|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/140168/3735|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140821000825/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/140168/3735|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 21, 2014|access-date=August 18, 2014|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=August 18, 2014}}</ref> On April 16, 2015, he was named to the [[EuroCup Basketball All-EuroCup Team|All-EuroCup Second Team]].<ref>{{cite news|title=2014-15 All-Eurocup first, second teams announced|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/5w4x8nukoug5cxca/2014-15-all-eurocup-first-second-teams-announced|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150417193341/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/5w4x8nukoug5cxca/2014-15-all-eurocup-first-second-teams-announced|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 17, 2015|access-date=July 26, 2015|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=April 16, 2015}}</ref> In July 2015, he re-signed with Lokomotiv.<ref>{{cite news|title=Anthony Randolph extends with Lokomotiv Kuban|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/euroleague/168380/anthony-randolph-extends-with-lokomotiv-kuban.html|access-date=July 26, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=July 12, 2015}}</ref> In his second season with Lokomotiv, he reached the [[2016 EuroLeague Final Four]], where his team lost in the semi-finals, but managed to win the third place game.

===Real Madrid (2016–2023)===
On July 15, 2016, Randolph signed a one-year deal with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Official Announcement: Randolph {{!}} Real Madrid CF|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2016/07/official-announcement-randolph|access-date=15 July 2016|work=Real Madrid C.F. - Web Oficial|date=15 July 2016|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Get to know Anthony Randolph {{!}} Real Madrid CF|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2016/07/get-to-know-anthony-randolph|access-date=15 July 2016|work=Real Madrid C.F. - Web Oficial|date=15 July 2016|language=en}}</ref>

On June 22, 2017, he re-signed with Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite news|title=Official Announcement: Anthony Randolph {{!}} Real Madrid CF|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/06/official-announcement-anthony-randolph|access-date=22 June 2017|work=Real Madrid C.F. - Web Oficial|date=22 June 2017|language=en}}</ref> In May 2018, Real Madrid won the [[2017–18 EuroLeague]] championship, after defeating [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe Doğuş]] in the [[2018 EuroLeague Final Four|final game]] 85–80.<ref name="EuroLeague18Champ">{{cite news|title=Real Madrid is 2018 EuroLeague champion|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=260&seasoncode=E2017#!report|access-date=20 May 2018|work=euroleague.net|date=20 May 2018}}</ref> Over 20 EuroLeague games, Randolph averaged 8.5 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.3 assists per game.

In February 2020, Randolph was sidelined with a fractured finger.<ref>{{cite news |title=Real Madrid's Anthony Randolph out with finger fracture |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/real-madrids-anthony-randolph-out-with-finger-fracture/ |website=Sportando |access-date=February 18, 2020 |date=February 18, 2020|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref>

On June 29, 2023, Randolph parted ways with the club after seven years and on December 13, 2024, he announced his retirement from basketball.<ref>{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Former NBA Forward Anthony Randolph Retires|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/12/former-nba-forward-anthony-randolph-retires.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=December 13, 2024|access-date=December 13, 2024}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:EuroBasket 2017 Finland vs Slovenia 55.jpg|200px|thumb|right|Randolph with Slovenia during [[EuroBasket 2017]], where he won the gold medal]]

===United States national team===
Randolph represented the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] at the [[Basketball at the 2015 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|2015 Pan American Games]], where he won a bronze medal.

===Slovenian national team===
On June 23, 2017, it was announced that Randolph would play for the senior [[Slovenia national basketball team|Slovenian national team]], after acquiring a Slovenian passport.<ref>{{cite news|title=Randolph joins Slovenia for EuroBasket|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/en/national-teams/469359/randolph-joins-slovenia-eurobasket/|access-date=June 23, 2017|work=Eurohoops.net|date=June 23, 2017}}</ref> On September 17, 2017, Slovenia defeated [[Serbian national basketball team|Serbia]], in the [[2017 EuroBasket]] [[EuroBasket 2017 Final|finals]], by a score of 93–85, and thereby claimed the title of EuroBasket champions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Slovenia crowned European champions for the first time |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/news/slovenia-crowned-european-champions-for-the-first-time |access-date=2022-07-05 |website=FIBA.basketball |date=September 17, 2017 |language=en}}</ref> Randolph was an important member of the team, as he averaged 11.7 points and 5.2 rebounds in 24.3 minutes of play.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony RANDOLPH at the FIBA EuroBasket 2017 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/player/Anthony-Randolph |access-date=2022-07-05 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}</ref>
